preamble: Monophthongizing [ai] to [i] means the nucleus takes on the quality of the high front offglide. In Akkadian, the Proto-Semitic diphthong *ay contracted to ī (*bayt- 'house' > bītum, *ʕayn- 'eye' > īnum), and *aw contracted to ū in the same way. Moroccan, Algerian and Tunisian Arabic made the same change independently, in contrast to the [eː] of Egyptian and Levantine Arabic: Classical bayt > Moroccan bīt 'room', zayt > zīt 'oil', ʕayn > ʕīn 'eye'.

examples.note: The pharyngeal was also lost; compare Hebrew ʿáyin and Arabic ʕayn.
Urban Moroccan monophthongizes ay to ī; some rural and conservative speech keeps bayt.
Compare Levantine and Hijazi zēt, which have [eː] instead.
The same ʕīn occurs in Algerian, Tunisian and Libyan Arabic.
